title: Train/test split
body:
Split the iris data into train and test sets with 25% for testing, random_state=0, stratified on y. Name them X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test and end with (X_train.shape, X_test.shape).

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=0, stratify=y)
(X_train.shape, X_test.shape)
hint: train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=0, stratify=y) returns four arrays in that order.

title: Fix the data leak
body:
This code scales the data before splitting, so the test set leaks into the scaler:

scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    scaler.transform(X), y, test_size=0.3, random_state=1, stratify=y)

Rewrite it so you split first (same arguments, on the raw X) and fit scaler on the training data only. End with scaler.mean_[:3].round(3).

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True)
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=1, stratify=y)
scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_train)
X_train_s, X_test_s = scaler.transform(X_train), scaler.transform(X_test)
scaler.mean_[:3].round(3)
hint: Swap the order: train_test_split on raw X, then StandardScaler().fit(X_train).

title: Build a pipeline
body:
Create a Pipeline with steps ("scale", StandardScaler()) and ("clf", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)), fit it on the breast cancer training set, and return test accuracy rounded to 3 decimals.

title: Categorical features
body:
Predict house price from city, sqft and beds. Use a ColumnTransformer that one-hot encodes city (with handle_unknown="ignore") and passes the numeric columns through, followed by LinearRegression. Fit on all of houses and return the predicted price for new_house, rounded to 1 decimal.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
houses = pd.DataFrame({
    'city': ['Austin', 'Austin', 'Denver', 'Denver', 'Boston', 'Boston', 'Austin', 'Denver', 'Boston', 'Austin', 'Denver', 'Boston'],
    'sqft': [1400, 2100, 1600, 2500, 1200, 1900, 1750, 1300, 2300, 2600, 2000, 1500],
    'beds': [3, 4, 3, 4, 2, 3, 3, 2, 4, 5, 3, 3],
    'price': [410, 590, 450, 690, 520, 760, 480, 380, 880, 700, 560, 610],   # thousands of dollars
})
new_house = pd.DataFrame({'city': ['Denver'], 'sqft': [1800], 'beds': [3]})
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
prep = ColumnTransformer([('city', OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore'), ['city'])], remainder='passthrough')
model = make_pipeline(prep, LinearRegression()).fit(houses[['city', 'sqft', 'beds']], houses['price'])
round(float(model.predict(new_house)[0]), 1)
hint: ColumnTransformer([("city", OneHotEncoder(...), ["city"])], remainder="passthrough"), then chain it with the regressor.

title: Choose model complexity
body:
For polynomial degrees 1 to 5, score a pipeline of PolynomialFeatures(degree) and LinearRegression with 5-fold cross-validation using scoring="neg_mean_squared_error" and KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=0). Return the degree with the best (highest) mean score.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(5)
x = np.sort(rng.uniform(-3, 3, 80)).reshape(-1, 1)
y = 0.5 * x[:, 0] ** 3 - x[:, 0] + rng.normal(0, 1.5, 80)
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline

cv = KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=0)
scores = {d: cross_val_score(make_pipeline(PolynomialFeatures(d), LinearRegression()), x, y, cv=cv, scoring='neg_mean_squared_error').mean() for d in range(1, 6)}
max(scores, key=scores.get)
hint: Loop over degrees, store the mean CV score of each, and pick the key with the largest value.

title: Failure rate by machine
body:
sensors holds 600 sensor snapshots from four machines, with failure = 1 when the machine failed within the next shift. Return the failure rate (share of snapshots with a failure) for each machine_id, rounded to 3 decimals.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(7)
n = 600
sensors = pd.DataFrame({
    'machine_id': rng.choice(['M1', 'M2', 'M3', 'M4'], n),
    'temp': rng.normal(70, 5, n).round(1),
    'vibration': rng.gamma(2.0, 0.5, n).round(3),
    'pressure': rng.normal(30, 3, n).round(2),
    'hours_since_service': rng.randint(0, 500, n),
})
risk = (0.04 * (sensors['temp'] - 70) + 1.5 * (sensors['vibration'] - 1)
        + 0.006 * (sensors['hours_since_service'] - 250)
        + 0.5 * (sensors['machine_id'] == 'M3'))
sensors['failure'] = (risk + rng.normal(0, 0.6, n) > 1.2).astype(int)
FEATURES = ['temp', 'vibration', 'pressure', 'hours_since_service']
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution: sensors.groupby('machine_id')['failure'].mean().round(3)
hint: The mean of a 0/1 column is a rate.

title: Process capability
body:
Using all 125 shaft diameters and the spec limits LSL, USL, compute Cp = (USL − LSL) / 6σ and Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL) / 3σ, with σ the sample standard deviation. Return (Cp, Cpk), each rounded to 3 decimals.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(3)
shafts = pd.DataFrame({'subgroup': np.repeat(np.arange(1, 26), 5),
                       'diameter': rng.normal(25.0, 0.012, 125).round(4)})
shafts.loc[shafts['subgroup'].between(18, 20), 'diameter'] += 0.025   # a tool shift
LSL, USL = 24.95, 25.05
A2 = 0.577   # control chart constant for subgroups of 5
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
mu = shafts['diameter'].mean()
sigma = shafts['diameter'].std()
cp = (USL - LSL) / (6 * sigma)
cpk = min(USL - mu, mu - LSL) / (3 * sigma)
(round(cp, 3), round(cpk, 3))
hint: pandas .std() is the sample standard deviation (ddof=1); numpy's np.std is not, by default.

title: X-bar chart limits
body:
For the shaft data (subgroups of 5), compute the subgroup means and ranges. The centre line is the mean of the subgroup means; the limits are CL ± A2 × R̄, where R̄ is the mean range. Return (LCL, CL, UCL), each rounded to 4 decimals.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(3)
shafts = pd.DataFrame({'subgroup': np.repeat(np.arange(1, 26), 5),
                       'diameter': rng.normal(25.0, 0.012, 125).round(4)})
shafts.loc[shafts['subgroup'].between(18, 20), 'diameter'] += 0.025   # a tool shift
LSL, USL = 24.95, 25.05
A2 = 0.577   # control chart constant for subgroups of 5
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
g = shafts.groupby('subgroup')['diameter']
means, ranges = g.mean(), g.max() - g.min()
cl, rbar = means.mean(), ranges.mean()
(round(cl - A2 * rbar, 4), round(cl, 4), round(cl + A2 * rbar, 4))
hint: Group by subgroup; range is max - min.

title: Out-of-control subgroups
body:
Using the X-bar limits from the shaft data (CL ± A2 × R̄), return a list of the subgroup numbers whose mean falls outside the limits, in order.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(3)
shafts = pd.DataFrame({'subgroup': np.repeat(np.arange(1, 26), 5),
                       'diameter': rng.normal(25.0, 0.012, 125).round(4)})
shafts.loc[shafts['subgroup'].between(18, 20), 'diameter'] += 0.025   # a tool shift
LSL, USL = 24.95, 25.05
A2 = 0.577   # control chart constant for subgroups of 5
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
g = shafts.groupby('subgroup')['diameter']
means, ranges = g.mean(), g.max() - g.min()
cl, rbar = means.mean(), ranges.mean()
means[(means > cl + A2 * rbar) | (means < cl - A2 * rbar)].index.tolist()
hint: Compute the limits, then filter the means Series with a boolean mask and take its index.

title: Detect temperature spikes
body:
temps is a 5-minute temperature series. Flag a reading as a spike when it exceeds the mean of the previous 12 readings plus 3 times their standard deviation. Return the number of spikes.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(11)
idx = pd.date_range('2025-03-03 00:00', periods=288, freq='5min')
temps = pd.Series(70 + np.sin(np.arange(288) / 30) * 2 + rng.normal(0, 0.4, 288), index=idx).round(2)
temps.iloc[[60, 150, 151, 240]] += [6.0, 5.0, 4.5, 7.0]   # spikes
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
roll = temps.rolling(12)
limit = (roll.mean() + 3 * roll.std()).shift(1)
int((temps > limit).sum())
hint: temps.rolling(12).mean() includes the current reading; .shift(1) makes it use only earlier ones.

title: Rare failures and class weights
body:
Failures are rare, so a plain model can miss them. Fit two pipelines of StandardScaler and LogisticRegression: one default, one with class_weight="balanced". Return (recall_default, recall_balanced) on the test set, each rounded to 3 decimals.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(7)
n = 600
sensors = pd.DataFrame({
    'machine_id': rng.choice(['M1', 'M2', 'M3', 'M4'], n),
    'temp': rng.normal(70, 5, n).round(1),
    'vibration': rng.gamma(2.0, 0.5, n).round(3),
    'pressure': rng.normal(30, 3, n).round(2),
    'hours_since_service': rng.randint(0, 500, n),
})
risk = (0.04 * (sensors['temp'] - 70) + 1.5 * (sensors['vibration'] - 1)
        + 0.006 * (sensors['hours_since_service'] - 250)
        + 0.5 * (sensors['machine_id'] == 'M3'))
sensors['failure'] = (risk + rng.normal(0, 0.6, n) > 1.2).astype(int)
FEATURES = ['temp', 'vibration', 'pressure', 'hours_since_service']
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    sensors[FEATURES], sensors['failure'], test_size=0.3, random_state=0, stratify=sensors['failure'])
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import recall_score
plain = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression()).fit(X_train, y_train)
bal = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced')).fit(X_train, y_train)
(round(recall_score(y_test, plain.predict(X_test)), 3), round(recall_score(y_test, bal.predict(X_test)), 3))
hint: LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced") reweights classes by their inverse frequency.

title: Unsupervised anomaly detection
body:
Fit IsolationForest(contamination=0.02, random_state=0) on temp, vibration and pressure. Return a list of the sensors index labels it flags as anomalies (prediction −1), in order.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(7)
n = 600
sensors = pd.DataFrame({
    'machine_id': rng.choice(['M1', 'M2', 'M3', 'M4'], n),
    'temp': rng.normal(70, 5, n).round(1),
    'vibration': rng.gamma(2.0, 0.5, n).round(3),
    'pressure': rng.normal(30, 3, n).round(2),
    'hours_since_service': rng.randint(0, 500, n),
})
risk = (0.04 * (sensors['temp'] - 70) + 1.5 * (sensors['vibration'] - 1)
        + 0.006 * (sensors['hours_since_service'] - 250)
        + 0.5 * (sensors['machine_id'] == 'M3'))
sensors['failure'] = (risk + rng.normal(0, 0.6, n) > 1.2).astype(int)
FEATURES = ['temp', 'vibration', 'pressure', 'hours_since_service']
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
cols = ['temp', 'vibration', 'pressure']
pred = IsolationForest(contamination=0.02, random_state=0).fit_predict(sensors[cols])
sensors.index[pred == -1].tolist()
hint: fit_predict returns 1 for normal points and −1 for anomalies.

title: Overall equipment effectiveness
body:
oee_log has three shifts per machine. Sum each machine's shifts first, then compute availability = (planned − downtime) / planned, performance = ideal_cycle_s × total_count / (run minutes × 60), quality = good_count / total_count, and OEE = availability × performance × quality. Return OEE per machine as a Series rounded to 3 decimals, highest first.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
m = oee_log.groupby('machine').agg(planned=('planned_min', 'sum'), down=('downtime_min', 'sum'),
                                     cycle=('ideal_cycle_s', 'first'), total=('total_count', 'sum'), good=('good_count', 'sum'))
run = m['planned'] - m['down']
oee = (run / m['planned']) * (m['cycle'] * m['total'] / (run * 60)) * (m['good'] / m['total'])
oee.round(3).sort_values(ascending=False)
hint: Aggregate with groupby().agg() first; the ideal cycle time is constant per machine.
